newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia police deny involvement in starting riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia police deny involvement in starting riot.

text.p: Indonesian police have denied allegations by the official National Commission on Human Rights they took sides in a political dispute that sparked riots in Jakarta on July 27, the Merdeka daily reported on Sunday.

Indonesia's official human rights watchdog on Saturday linked security forces to the start of riots regarded as the worst in the capital in more than 20 years. Five people died and 149 were injured in the violence, the commisson said.
"We do not take sides with anybody," national police spokesman Brigadier-General Nurfaizi was quoted as saying.
"What is found in the field that can be supported by proof will be taken to court. The Indonesian police are not discriminative in upholding the law," Nurfaizi said.

In its final official report on the July 27 incident, the commission said 23 people were still missing and called on the authorities to continue to search for them and determine whether they were alive or dead.

It said there were two phases to the events: a factional assault backed by the security forces on the headquarters of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), and subsequent rioting which it said was influenced by the violent takeover of the PDI building.

The assault on the headquarters followed a rebel PDI congress financed by the government in the north Sumatran city of Medan in June, in which Megawati Sukarnoputri was ousted as party leader by parliamentary deputy speaker Surjadi.

"The takeover of the (PDI) secretariat on July 27 was an action that was carried out violently by the executive board of the Medan congress and a group of its supporters, together with the security forces," the report said.

Witnesses reported at the time how riot police stood by as about 200 young men wearing T-shirts saying they were supporters of the Medan congress attacked the headquarters with stones. Television footage of the scene was broadcast worldwide.
Nurfaizi said police needed the names of Surjadi supporters as well as witnesses. "We need proof," he said.
The commission said officials of Surjadi's faction had refused to hand over the names of the 200 people they described as being from their "security unit".
Last Wednesday, 64 of 124 people arrested in and around the party headquarters went on trial. Lawyers say all are members or supporters of Megawati's faction of the PDI.
The commission called on the government not to discriminate and to take legal action against the 200 Surjadi supporters who attacked the office.
